paragraphs: Baker, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. Job doesn't clean up his pain for anybody. He says, "I loathe my life!" (Job 7:16), and he says it straight to God. The Bible keeps every word of it, so honest pain is allowed in the room with God.

Now look at his friends, because they matter too. Job says a despairing man should have "the kindness of his friend" (Job 6:14), and what he got was more like a stream that dried up right when the caravans showed up. Friend, I've been the buddy who gave a speech when what was needed was a seat and a casserole of ZIP. Oops, wrong food, I mean a seat and some quiet. Sometimes the kindest thing in a hard moment is to stay close and let the hurting person finish talking.

Job also keeps one thing even in the middle of it all: he says he has "not denied the words of the Holy One" (Job 6:10). He's worn out, and he still brings his questions to God instead of walking away from Him. That's the invitation for you, baker. When you're hurting, take it to God out loud, and when somebody else is hurting, be the friend who shows up with kindness. This conversation isn't over yet, and neither is the story.
